H4NY16087.name: George Latimer
H4NY16087.bio: Former Westchester County Executive with more than three decades in public office.

positions.stance: Calls affordable housing "a fundamental human right"; will push to incentivize affordable housing construction, protect renters' rights, and expand homeownership for low and middle-income families.
"Staunchly supports protecting reproductive freedoms" and would vote for the Women's Health Protection Act to secure clinic access and providers.
Will prioritize funding to repair and modernize roads, bridges, and mass transit, and resilient stormwater and sewer systems.
Advocates "common-sense gun reform including an assault weapons ban and universal background checks," violence prevention programs, and Extreme Risk Protection Orders.
Supports more aid to Ukraine, stands with Israel while advocating a two-state solution, and fully supports NATO and the security of Pacific allies.

H4NY07052.name: Joseph Cinquemani
H4NY07052.bio: Attorney with a 32-year law practice focused on real estate, business transactions, and succession planning.

positions.stance: Proposes expanding the federal tax withholding exemption.
Proposes "a 3-part healthcare insurance solution: Inform – Expand – Deregulate."
Proposes recommissioning the Indian Point Energy Center for small modular reactors (SMR).
Proposes a "Billionaire Investment Tax – A BIT for Unions."
Wants "state & local law enforcement to cooperate with federal law officers."

H2NY17162.name: Mike Lawler
H2NY17162.bio: U.S. Representative for New York's 17th District since 2023 and former New York State Assembly member.

positions.stance: Touts quadrupling the SALT deduction cap to $40,000, expanding the Child Tax Credit, and eliminating taxes on Social Security for most seniors and on tips and overtime.
Pushed for a House vote on extending Affordable Care Act subsidies, introduced an IVF tax credit bill, and opposes cuts to Medicare physician payments.
Supports protecting Social Security and Medicare, Medicaid work requirements for able-bodied adults without children, and championed the Social Security Fairness Act.
Advocates reopening Indian Point, an "all-of-the-above energy strategy," expanded natural gas infrastructure, and repealing or overhauling New York's CLCPA.
Opposes the "defund the police" agenda, wants cashless bail laws repealed with a dangerousness standard, and supports federal funding for local law enforcement.

H6NY17171.name: Cait Conley
H6NY17171.bio: Former active-duty Army officer of 16 years, former Director for Counterterrorism on the National Security Council, and former official at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

positions.stance: Wants to lower drug costs and premiums by "holding Big Pharma and insurance companies accountable and creating a public option for health insurance."
Supports banning members of Congress and the White House from trading stocks "so they can't get rich when the companies they invest in raise our prices."
Wants to cut utility bills by holding monopoly utilities accountable, tying profits to performance, and banning pass-through costs to ratepayers for jets, lobbying, and campaign donations.
Supports affordable childcare through subsidies and tax credits, universal pre-K, expanded CTE and apprenticeships, capped student loan rates, and opposes school vouchers.
Supports federal investment in Hudson Valley energy, water, sewer and transportation infrastructure, cutting red tape for renewable projects, and holding electric utilities accountable.

H8NY19223.name: Pat Ryan
H8NY19223.bio: U.S. Representative, former Ulster County Executive, Army intelligence officer who served two combat tours in Iraq, and founder of a technology company.

positions.stance: Fighting to lower costs by taking on price-gouging monopolies, supports breaking up UnitedHealth and Optum, and introduced a Housing Affordability Agenda to build more housing.
Wants billionaires and corporations to pay their fair share, tax relief for the middle class, paid family leave for all Americans, and equal pay for equal work.
Supports "commonsense gun reforms including red flag laws, an assault weapons ban, and universal background checks," plus more mental health and addiction recovery resources.
Opposes a national abortion ban, wants to re-establish Roe v. Wade protections, and supports the John Lewis Voting Rights Act.
Supports investment in electric public transportation and green job training, PFAS cleanup in drinking water, and his Hudson River Protection Act banning polluting barges.
Will address "taxes, energy costs, everyday expenses, and healthcare costs to ensure more income stays with Hudson Valley families and small businesses."
Focuses on "good-paying jobs, small business growth, skilled trades, and education connected to careers in the region."
Promotes "congressional ethics, government transparency, and protecting the rights and public safety of local residents."

H8NY22177.name: Josh Riley
H8NY22177.bio: Attorney; former counsel on the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee, fellow on the Senate labor committee staff, and policy analyst at the U.S. Department of Labor.

positions.stance: Wants to hold utilities accountable by fighting rate hikes, banning foreign ownership of American utilities, blocking CEO bonuses, and requiring Big Tech to pay for data-center grid upgrades.
Backs the Equality Act "to ban anti-LGBTQ+ discrimination nationwide" and supports mental health and suicide prevention services for LGBTQ+ youth.
Fighting to fully fund special education, eliminate waiting periods for Social Security Disability Insurance and Medicare benefits, and raise outdated SSI asset limits.
Supports a larger Child Tax Credit, tax-deductible utility fees, eliminating federal taxes on Social Security benefits, and fully deductible union dues and work expenses.
Says "women's healthcare decisions are women's healthcare decisions"; supports the Women's Health Protection Act to restore Roe v. Wade and protecting birth control access.

H6NY19268.name: Peter Oberacker
H6NY19268.bio: New York State Senator, former town supervisor and county representative, food scientist, and founder of the food innovation company FormTech Solutions.

H8NY21203.name: Paul Tonko
H8NY21203.bio: U.S. Representative for the Capital Region since 2009, engineer, former President and CEO of NYSERDA, and former New York State Assembly member.

positions.stance: Says affordable health care is critical and calls for fixing "the parts of the ACA that don't work while moving forward with the provisions that do."
Calls fighting climate change a top global security threat and says it "will also bring stable and good paying jobs" to the Capital Region.
Says the nation must be built back "STRONGER" after the pandemic and pledges continued support for those who need it as the American Rescue Act takes effect.
Committed to "the right to collectively bargain and form a union," living wages at all levels, and access to skill development programs.
Says long-ignored and under-served communities must have equal access to opportunities for long-term success "regardless of race, gender, or anything."

H6NY20225.name: Ralph Ambrosio
H6NY20225.bio: Attorney in private practice; former U.S. Navy member, New York State Police member and assistant counsel, assistant district attorney, public defender, and assistant attorney general.

positions.stance: Wants to tackle "crushing costs and lack of opportunity through tax cutting and deregulation."
Will push an "all-of-the-above energy strategy that will produce abundant supply while driving down costs."
Supports law enforcement, securing the nation and borders, "defending the right to self-defense," and focusing on crime prevention and effective policing.
Supports "term limits, Voter ID, parental rights in education, and rooting out corruption wherever it exists."

H6NY21157.name: Anthony Constantino
H6NY21157.bio: CEO and founder of the online printing company Sticker Mule.

positions.stance: Pledges to "put more money in your pockets," saying as a CEO he is best at eliminating waste and growing the economy.
Wants to "bring reliable high-speed internet and cell coverage to the North Country" to attract remote jobs and grow online businesses.
Would cut and oppose regulations that drive up prices, "including insane food, restaurant, and green energy regulations."
Would work with President Trump "to stop drugs, crime, terrorism, and low-wage labor from crossing our northern border."
Wants to "end the unfair solar farm deals, secure a farm bill that helps all farmers equally, and cut burdensome farming regulations."
Supports repealing unnecessary regulations, fair trade deals, bringing back American manufacturing, and strengthening supply chains to lower costs and protect seniors.
Wants to "make it harder to enter our country illegally, but easier to enter legally," hire more Border Patrol agents, and fix H-2A and H-2B guest worker programs.
Supports cutting burdensome regulations, investing in roads, bridges and rural broadband, and expanding vocational and trade school programs like BOCES.
"I will never vote to cut Social Security, Medicare, or Medicaid"; supports telehealth, lower drug costs, and abortion access, opposing total abortion bans.
Supports expanded VA services and mental health care, mobile VA clinics, a 24/7 hotline, and stronger community care programs for veterans.

H4NY22085.name: John Mannion
H4NY22085.bio: U.S. Representative, former New York State Senator, and public high school biology and chemistry teacher for almost 30 years.

positions.stance: Says the wealthiest Americans "should pay their fair share in taxes," wants large companies to pay for their energy use, and cosponsors a grocery price-gouging bill.
Supports increased federal funding for public schools, expanding universal pre-K, and improved teacher pay, benefits, and working conditions.
Supports reducing greenhouse gas emissions, the New York-New Jersey Watershed Protection Act, and conservation grants to protect wildlife and wetlands.
Wants to restore Medicare and Medicaid cuts, restore ACA tax credits, supports a universal public option, lower drug prices, and the Women's Health Protection Act.
Supports community project funding for law enforcement, bipartisan online child-protection legislation, and the Enhanced Background Checks Act of 2025.

H6NY22213.name: Kailee Buller
H6NY22213.bio: Former Chief of Staff to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Agriculture and former chief executive officer.

positions.stance: Running "to restore opportunity and affordability," focusing on growing good-paying jobs and lowering everyday costs so families need not leave New York.
Supports employer childcare tax credits and grants, a stronger Child Care Tax Credit, and an expanded Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit ending the marriage penalty.
Supports "repealing those costly climate mandates and advancing an all-of-the-above energy policy" to lower prices and strengthen reliability.
Supports policies that increase housing supply, encourage responsible development, cut unnecessary regulations, and make it easier for first-time buyers to enter the market.
Will "fight to protect family farms, reduce red tape, and ensure agriculture remains a strong and viable industry in Central New York."

H2NY23228.name: Nick Langworthy
H2NY23228.bio: Former chairman of the New York State Republican Party and the Erie County Republican Party, and former congressional district director.

positions.stance: Wants to curb wasteful government spending and use "pro-growth tax and deregulatory policies" to raise take-home pay and create jobs.
Wants to maximize American-made energy production and "cut the permitting process time in half" to lower gas and utility costs.
Wants to "move supply chains away from China, expand U.S. manufacturing," and enhance economic competitiveness and cyber resiliency.
Supports fully funding border enforcement, ending catch-and-release loopholes, requiring legal status to get a job, and eliminating welfare incentives.
Supports 200,000 more police officers, opposes efforts to defund police, and would permanently criminalize all forms of illicit fentanyl.
Supports "a universal healthcare system that guarantees stable, accessible, cost-effective basic care for every American," lower drug costs, and protecting rural hospitals.
Will work with county and local governments to make it easier to build housing, expand supply to drive down costs, and support community redevelopment.
Supports universal free school meals, protecting funding for rural schools, special education and workforce training, and regulating AI to serve the common good.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage "to $15 immediately," strengthening unions, and banning price discrimination that hurts small businesses.
Supports fair pricing and stable markets for local agriculture, sustainable farming practices, and regional food systems that keep dollars local.

H4NY22051.name: Claudia Tenney
H4NY22051.bio: Attorney, co-owner of the commercial printing firm Mid-York Press, U.S. Representative first elected in 2016, and former New York State Assembly member.

positions.stance: Says she has been a leader against "Chinese theft of American intellectual property" and a proponent of breaking China's grip on the U.S. financial system.
Supports rolling back business-burdening regulations and will "oppose all unnecessary and burdensome regulations and taxes on businesses and individuals."
Works to ensure the Veterans Administration delivers "proper and timely healthcare services" veterans were promised.
Believes the right to bear arms "shall not be infringed," opposes unproven gun control on law-abiding owners, and sought repeal of New York's SAFE Act.
Fighting for "free-market, patient-centric healthcare" that lets New Yorkers choose affordable insurance and keep their doctor.

H6NY24219.name: Alissa Ellman
H6NY24219.bio: Combat veteran who served overseas, including at Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan.

positions.stance: Supports expanding affordable childcare, supporting small businesses, investing in home repair programs, and expanding the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit.
Will fight for funding to expand rural bus networks and secure federal funding to modernize water systems and repair aging infrastructure.
Has "long supported LGBTQ+ rights, reproductive freedom, and equal rights for all Americans."
Supports passing the PRO Act, ending right-to-work laws, and preventing abuse of the "independent contractor" loophole.

H8NY25105.name: Joseph Morelle
H8NY25105.bio: U.S. Representative; former Majority Leader of the New York State Assembly and former Monroe County legislator.

positions.stance: Believes "access to health care is a fundamental human right"; supports lower drug costs, a $35 monthly insulin cap, and expanded ACA premium tax credits.
"Stands firmly against efforts to restrict reproductive freedom"; supports protecting contraception access, a federal right to IVF, and better maternal health outcomes.
Says we must "protect Social Security and Medicare, no matter what"; supports increasing Social Security benefits and investing in home and community-based care.
Supports a price on carbon with revenue returned to families, protections against environmental discrimination, and reducing single-use plastic waste.
Believes veterans must have access to the care and benefits they earned; supports VA caregiver benefits and grants for veteran benefits outreach.

H6NY25208.name: Virginia McIntyre
H6NY25208.bio: Monroe County Legislator, educator, entrepreneur, and former international language professor and interpreter.

positions.stance: Supports "community policing, prevention programs, and strong partnerships that reduce violence and build trust."
Wants to "expand opportunity with accountability, vocational and technical education, and pathways to good careers."
Wants to "grow good-paying jobs, support small business, and reduce the burden on working families."
Wants to "fix roads and bridges, expand broadband, and invest responsibly to create jobs and improve quality of life."
Supports pricing transparency, fair billing, and holding insurers and hospitals accountable "so families can afford care without surprises."

H4NY26078.name: Tim Kennedy
H4NY26078.bio: U.S. Representative and former New York State Senator.

positions.stance: Opposes politicization of the civil service and tariffs he says will cost jobs, and supports legislation to stop union-busting.
Will keep fighting to protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid and supports strengthening them to make health care more affordable and accessible.
Supports "a woman's right to make her own health care decisions," believes diversity is our greatest strength, and opposes discrimination.
Sponsors legislation to ban assault weapons and military-grade body armor and to give local law enforcement the resources to keep dangerous weapons off streets.
"Strongly believes in the checks and balances between the branches of government articulated in the Constitution."

Supports local-federal agency cooperation grants, immigration enforcement prioritizing serious public safety threats, worksite hiring compliance, and aggressively disrupting fentanyl trafficking networks.
Supports tax rebates for working families, lower drug and health costs including pharmacy benefit manager reform, and less red tape on energy leases.
Supports stronger online privacy protections for kids and limits on AI content involving minors, says "no child is born into the wrong body," and backs capital punishment for convicted child rapists.

H6PA08277.name: Brian Fitzpatrick
H6PA08277.bio: U.S. Representative; former FBI Supervisory Special Agent and federal prosecutor.

positions.stance: Authored the INTERDICT Act against fentanyl, supported $25 billion for border security, and backs tougher penalties for repeat criminal illegal immigrants and online predators.
Supports a simpler, fairer tax code, Made in America initiatives, repealing outdated regulations, and reforming "unfair trade deals that put the American worker at a disadvantage."
Supports term limits, abolishing congressional pensions, a Balanced-Budget Amendment, and his "No Budget, No Pay" legislation.
Will "fight to protect and strengthen these programs"; supports eliminating income taxes on Social Security benefits and an enhanced cost-of-living adjustment.
Says everyone should have affordable insurance; supports lower drug prices, protections for preexisting conditions, and protecting Medicaid and CHIP.

H6PA01181.name: Bob Harvie
H6PA01181.bio: Bucks County Commissioner, former Falls Township supervisor, and former public high school social studies teacher of 26 years.

positions.stance: Says healthcare "should be a right"; supports restoring ACA tax credits, lowering the Medicare buy-in age to 55, and expanding Medicare drug price negotiation.
Will fight for a middle class tax cut "while ensuring large corporations and the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share."
Will fight to overturn Citizens United and "permanently ban corporate PAC contributions"; pledges to take no corporate PAC money.
Wants to roll back tariffs that raise food and household costs and "raise the minimum wage to $15 per hour."
Supports "a complete ban on congressional stock trading," extended to federal judges, executive branch members, and Senate-confirmed officials.

H4PA13199.name: Brendan Boyle
H4PA13199.bio: U.S. Representative since 2015 and member of the House Budget and Ways and Means Committees.

H6PA02205.name: Jessica Arriaga
H6PA02205.bio: Healthcare professional with more than 20 years of experience working in operating rooms.

positions.stance: Will seek federal resources to help police target repeat violent offenders, expand community prevention programs, and fund mental health and addiction services.
Supports reducing the tax burden on working families, cutting unnecessary federal regulations on small businesses, and expanding job training tied to local employers.
Will fight for federal support for career and technical education, workforce training, school safety, and school-union-employer partnerships.
Will work to expand access to affordable care, reduce costs, increase price transparency, and cut bureaucratic barriers that delay treatment.
Will support stronger oversight, fight wasteful spending, and push for transparency in how federal resources are allocated to cities.

H6PA03203.name: Chris Rabb
H6PA03203.bio: Pennsylvania state representative first elected in 2016.

positions.stance: Calls for guaranteeing "homes for everyone through Housing First Model."
Supports "universal basic income and a living wage for all" to tackle the affordability crisis.
Lists "Protecting Reproductive Freedom" among his top affordability priorities.
Supports "regional food stability and national grocery stores."
Says "real safety comes from strong communities, not over-policing or over-prosecuting"; supports mental health responders, ending the War on Drugs, and abolishing the death penalty.

H8PA04116.name: Madeleine Dean
H8PA04116.bio: U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 4th District, lawyer, and former La Salle University professor.

positions.stance: Says "affordable, quality healthcare must be a right"; supports protecting and expanding Medicare and Medicaid, extending ACA tax credits, and lowering drug prices.
Opposes "massive tax cuts for the wealthy" and the President's tariff policies; supports manufacturing, infrastructure investment, and a $35 Medicare insulin cap.
Demands accountability by asserting Congress's Article I powers, protecting checks and balances, and "restoring the independence of the Justice Department."
Supports a strong legal immigration system, a path to citizenship, asylum for those who need it, and reinstating DACA.
Supports broadening anti-discrimination laws, enforcing ADA requirements, the Equality Act, and reforming the criminal justice system.

H6PA04169.name: Aurora Stuski
H6PA04169.bio: Local business owner in West Norriton.

positions.stance: Wants to modernize Social Security so working seniors are not penalized, expand senior property tax relief, and increase affordable housing for veterans.
Wants residents given first opportunity to buy manufactured home communities when sold and protected from "excessive or predatory lot rent increases."
Supports reducing permitting delays, mixed-income housing near existing infrastructure, and adaptive reuse of vacant commercial properties.
Proposes a Youth Support and Opportunity Network, an early intervention system to reduce foster care placements, youth homelessness, and juvenile justice involvement.
Wants to "spend taxpayer dollars earlier and smarter" by investing in prevention, such as early behavioral health treatment and stable housing.

H8PA07200.name: Mary Gay Scanlon
H8PA07200.bio: U.S. Representative since 2018; former pro bono counsel at Ballard Spahr, Education Law Center staff attorney, and Wallingford-Swarthmore School Board member.
